Chapter 10: Embedding the Practices for Long-Term Impact
So, how do you make sure these practices become second nature for your team?
The real magic happens when these habits aren’t just something you do—they’re part of who you are as a team. It’s about weaving them into your daily routines, your rituals, and even your systems. That way, they stick around, no matter who’s leading or how things change.
Let’s talk about a few ways to really embed these practices for the long haul.
First, try ritualizing check-ins. Make those regular one-on-ones, team huddles, or feedback sessions a non-negotiable part of everyone’s week. When they’re on the calendar, they’re real—and people start to count on them.
Next, think about documenting your values and norms. Work together to create a simple team charter or set of agreements that reflect the practices you want to live by. It doesn’t have to be fancy—just something everyone understands and believes in.
Another powerful move? Peer recognition. Don’t let all the appreciation come from just the manager. Encourage team members to call out each other’s strengths and wins. It builds trust and shows everyone that their efforts matter.
And when someone new joins the team, make the culture clear from day one. Use your onboarding and training as a way to show, not just tell, what your team values. Let new hires see the practices in action right away.
Here’s a real-world example—one software company put together a “culture playbook.” Inside, they spelled out how the team listens, gives feedback, supports growth, and celebrates together. This living document helped everyone, whether they’d just joined or had been around for years, stay on the same page as the team grew and evolved.
Over time, when these practices are truly embedded, something amazing happens. They start to reinforce themselves. New leaders step up naturally, team members hold each other accountable, and the culture stays strong—even through change and transition.
The manager’s role? It shifts from being the only driver to acting as a steward—guiding, supporting, and trusting the team to keep the flame burning.
That’s how you build a culture that lifts everyone, for the long run.
